div.head: II Cn 11
div.ab: ⁊ smeage man symle on æghwylce wisan, hu man fyrmest mæge ræd aredian þeode to þearfe ⁊ rihtne Cristendom swyðost aræran ⁊ æghwylce unlage geornost afyllan.
And smeaga man symle on æghwilce wisan, hu man fyrmest mege ræd aredian ðeode to þearfe ⁊ rihtne Cristendom swyðost árærron ⁊ æghwilce unlaga geornnod afyllan.
Et perquiramus simul modis omnibus, quomodo precipuum possit consilium optineri ad profectum populi, rectaque Christianitas propensius erigi, quicquid iniustum est sollertius eneruari.
⁊ smeage man georne on æghwylce wísan, hu man fyrmæst mǽge rǽd aredian ðeode to ðearfe ⁊ rihtne Cristendóm swiðast arǽran ⁊ æghwylce unlage georne afyllen.
And thought shall diligently be taken in every way how best to determine what is advisable for the public good, and how best to promote true Christianity and diligently suppress every injustice.

Und man sinne immer (eifrig B) auf jede Weise, wie man zuvörderst dem Volke zum Nutzen einen vortheilhaften Plan ausfindig machen könne und rechtes Christenthum höchlichst aufrichten und jede Rechtswidrigkeit eifrigst (-ig B) abschaffen.

And let people always (eagerly, B) consider in every way how they can first devise a beneficial plan for the good of the people, and most highly exalt true Christianity, and most (eagerly, B) abolish every abuse of law.
div.note: A's ‘geornnod’ is perhaps a slip for ‘geornost’. Liebermann compares VI Atr 40.
